newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-LOLA TO MISS BRAZILIAN GRAND PRIX.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-LOLA TO MISS BRAZILIAN GRAND PRIX.

text.p: The Lola Formula One motor racing team on Wednesday withdrew from this weekend's Brazilian Grand Prix at Interlagos just two days before the start of practice because of "financial and technical problems.".

The team's two cars, driven by Brazilian Ricardo Rosset and Italian Vincenzo Sospiri, will be flown back to their factory in England and it is unclear whether they will take any further part in the season's competition.
A spokesman for the team said: "The team are returning here because of a few operation problems -- both technical and financial. We are just holding the situation at the moment."

Although the spokesman made it clear the team intended to take part in the next round of the world championship, the Argentine Grand Prix on April 13, it is very rare for teams to return to the sport after missing an event because of the financial penalties imposed.

Neither of the Ford-powered cars managed to qualify for the Australian Grand Prix three weeks ago, although team founder and principal Eric Broadley said last week that he was confident they would have qualified at Interlagos.
"I was disappointed that we did not race in Australia, but not entirely surprised," he said. "I have no doubt that we will qualify in Brazil and then begin to work our way up the grid."

Traditionally a chassis manufacturer, Lola entered their own team for the first time this season with a budget of $35 million. They had hoped to switch to their own engines mid-way through the season.
Founded in 1958 they last competed in Formula One in the 1993 season as part of the BMS Lola Ferrari team.
They have only one Formula One victory to their name -- the 1967 Italian Grand Prix -- but have a long and distinguished history in other racing, including IndyCar, Formula 3000 and Le Mans.
The move back into Formula One was announced in November but Broadley said in January: "It is exciting for us to be involved in Formula One but we are not going in with over-optimistic expectations."
